question.problem:
The center of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+6x+8y=-1$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}+6x+8y & =-1 \\ {x}^{2}+6x\,-\,4{y}^{2}+8y & =-1 \\ [{x}^{2}+6x]\,-\,4[{y}^{2}-2y] & =-1 \\ [(x+3)^{2}-9]\,-\,4[(y-1)^{2}-1] & =-1 \\ (x+3)^{2}-9\,-\,4(y-1)^{2}+4 & =-1 \\ (x+3)^{2}-4(y-1)^{2} & =-1+9-4 \\ (x+3)^{2}-4(y-1)^{2} & =4 \\ \frac{(x-(-3))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,-3,1\,).$
